281503031.description:
Hemingray Glass Company
No. 55 Transposition Insulator (CD 205)
Pressed Glass, Aqua Blue, Vintage Early to Mid-20th Century
Vintage Hemingray No. 55 CD 205 aqua glass transposition insulator, historically utilized on rural telephone and power transmission lines to rotate and swap wire positions to minimize electrical crosstalk interference. Manufactured in Muncie, Indiana, this distinctive style of American industrial glass remains a popular favorite among telegraph, utility, and antique glass collectors.
Distinctive transposition profile featuring spiral wire guide channels across the upper dome
Pressed aqua blue glass containing natural manufacturing swirl patterns and authentic seed air bubbles
Embossed "HEMINGRAY" on the front skirt and "N 55" on the reverse skirt, featuring a smooth base rim
Measures approximately 4 inches in diameter by 4 inches in height
Condition:
Embossed lettering remains crisp and well-defined. Glass exhibits brilliant gloss with typical factory mold seams and minor light surface contact marks consistent with authentic utility use. A minor fleabite flake is present on the edge of the interior skirt rim. Free of major cracks, repairs, or structural breaks.
Thank you for all of your support!

Artist Seated on Stump With Palette and Pipe
Hand-Painted Porcelain, 7.5 Inches Tall

The character study features charming sculpted details, including a classic yellow beret, green scarf, patched trousers, a pipe held in hand, and a painter's palette with dabs of color and brushes.
Figural porcelain statue of a bohemian artist seated on a tree stump
Accented with a painter's palette, paintbrushes, and smoking pipe
Detailed character sculpting with hand-painted finish in muted tones
